name: Fintech transaction restriction and enhanced-verification pathway

attribution.legal_posture: First-party provider descriptions of controls adopted in response to government warnings; they document provider controls rather than observed DPRK case evidence, an enforcement action, or an adjudication.

caveats: Cryptocurrency payment, off-platform work, language, pricing, reluctance to use video, and other listed signs are non-exclusive; identity, nationality, sanctions status, fraud, and wrongdoing require independent evidence.
Restrictions and enhanced verification should be proportionate, privacy-preserving, accessible, and subject to documented human review and independent corroboration.
The English and Japanese pages are language companions with displayed dates one day apart; they form one source family rather than independent corroboration.
The provider reports no identifying, restricting, reporting, or offboarding of a DPRK-linked account or transaction.
The provider statement documents a control pathway; product efficacy and measured detection require separate evidence.
This customer guidance implements a government warning; it provides policy context, with observed DPRK case evidence outside this record.

infrastructure.statement: Revolut Japan states that activity its systems identify as suspicious may result in transaction restrictions and requests for additional identity-verification material or documents explaining the transaction. Its English and Japanese notices are companion versions of one provider disclosure, not two independent confirmations and not evidence of a detected DPRK-linked account or payment.

sources.support: Revolut Japan asks customers to verify counterparties and whether a transaction would transfer funds to a DPRK IT worker. It lists cryptocurrency-payment or off-platform-work demands among non-exclusive signs, alongside identity and interaction inconsistencies. It says suspicious activity detected by its in-app systems may lead to transaction restrictions and requests for additional identity-verification documents or transaction information. Evidence boundary: The page is customer guidance and a general description of possible platform controls. It does not say Revolut detected a DPRK-linked account or transaction, and the listed signs are not proof individually
sources.locator: How do I stay protected; Signs to look out for

sources.support: The Japanese version says detected suspicious accounts or transactions may be restricted and customers may be asked for added identity verification or documents showing transaction content. Evidence boundary: This is the Japanese-language companion to the English page, with a one-day displayed publication-date difference. It is one logical disclosure, not independent corroboration or a disclosed incident
